title: Critères néerlandais pour l'hypercholestérolémie familiale (FH)
formula:
| Criteria | Points |
| --- | --- |
| Family history | |
| First-degree relative with known premature* coronary and vascular disease, OR First-degree relative with known LDL-C level above the 95th percentile for age and sex | 1 |
| First-degree relative with tendinous xanthomata and/or arcus cornealis, OR Children <18 years with LDL-C level above the 95th percentile for age and sex | 2 |
| Clinical history | |
| Patient with premature* coronary artery disease | 2 |
| Patient with premature* cerebral or peripheral vascular disease | 1 |
| Physical examination | |
| Tendinous xanthomata | 6 |
| Arcus cornealis prior to age 45 years | 4 |
| Cholesterol level, mmol/L (mg/dL) | |
| LDL-C ≥8.5 (330) LDL-C 6.5 - 8.4 (250 - 329) LDL-C 5.0 - 6.4 (190 - 249) LDL-C 4.0 - 4.9 (155 - 189) | 8 5 3 1 |
| DNA analysis | |
| Functional mutation of LDLR, apoB or PCSK9 gene | 8 |

*Premature = <55 years in men; <60 years in women.

From the[National Lipid Association Resource Center](https://nlaresourcecenter.lipidjournal.com/Content/PDFs/Tables/4.pdf).

how_to_use.why:
- Approche standardisée approuvée par les principales sociétés européennes de cardiologie.
- Intègre de multiples sources de données pour un diagnostic plus robuste que les critères fondés sur un seul paramètre.
- Facilite la recherche en fournissant des définitions diagnostiques cohérentes entre les études.
- Guide les décisions de tests génétiques en stratifiant la probabilité pré-test.
- Permet la stratification du risque et les décisions d’intensité thérapeutique.
- Largement validée dans des populations et des contextes cliniques divers.
how_to_use.when:
- Adultes avec suspicion de FH, en particulier ceux présentant :
  - Un cholestérol LDL élevé (généralement >190 mg/dL ou >4,9 mmol/L).
  - Des antécédents familiaux de maladie cardiovasculaire précoce ou d'hypercholestérolémie.
  - Des signes physiques évocateurs de FH (xanthomes tendineux, arc cornéen).
  - Une identification du cas index en milieu clinique.
- NON recommandé pour le dépistage en cascade des membres de la famille en raison d'un biais d'ascertainment.
how_to_use.pearls:
**Pearls:**

- Tends to be more comprehensive than other criteria by incorporating multiple clinical domains.
- Genetic testing provides the highest point value (8 points), allowing definite diagnosis even with lower LDL-C.
- Validated against genetic testing with reasonable discriminatory power.
- Allows for graded diagnostic certainty.

**Pitfalls:**

- High specificity but low sensitivity - better at confirming FH than screening for it.
- Physical signs are rare in modern practice: xanthomas present in <15% and corneal arcus in ~30% of genetically confirmed FH patients.
- Compromised by prior lipid-lowering therapy - requires estimation of untreated LDL-C levels.
- Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] can inflate scores and reduce genetic confirmation rates (e.g., in "definite" category, genetic FH confirmed in 71% when Lp(a) <75 mg/dL vs. only 50% when Lp(a) ≥75 mg/dL).
- Family history may be unreliable or unavailable.
- Should not be used for cascade screening of relatives due to ascertainment bias.
- Substantial proportion lack identifiable mutations even with high scores - up to two-thirds of clinically suspected cases remain genetically unexplained.

next_steps.advice:
- Utiliser toujours les valeurs de LDL-C non traité lorsque c'est possible.
- Envisager un test génétique pour tous les patients ayant un score ≥3 points, en particulier ceux avec une FH probable ou certaine.
- Documenter soigneusement l'examen physique à la recherche de xanthomes tendineux (notamment les tendons d'Achille, les tendons
next_steps.critical_actions:
- Exclude secondary causes of hypercholesterolemia before diagnosing FH (hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, obstructive liver disease).
- Initiate high-intensity statin therapy promptly - earlier treatment provides greater lifetime benefit due to cumulative LDL exposure.
- Pursue genetic testing for probable/definite FH to confirm diagnosis and enable cascade screening.
- Screen first-degree relatives - 50% will have FH if index case is confirmed.
- Measure Lp(a) to identify patients with combined risk and avoid misclassification. Elevated Lp(a) can mimic FH phenotype.
- Escalate therapy if LDL-C goals not met with statin + ezetimibe - most FH patients require combination therapy.
- Monitor for ASCVD with appropriate risk assessment and imaging when indicated.
next_steps.management:
Once FH is diagnosed using DLCN criteria (probable or definite), manage patients according to most recent AHA/ESC/EAS guidelines.

The following LDL-C target goals should be considered within individual clinical contexts:

- **Patients without ASCVD** : LDL-C <70 mg/dL (<1.8 mmol/L) for.
- **Patients with established ASCVD** : LDL-C <55 mg/dL (<1.4 mmol/L).

**Pharmacologic Options**

- First-line: Consider high-intensity statin (rosuvastatin 40 mg or atorvastatin 80 mg daily) - reduces LDL-C by 50-60%.
- Second-line: Consider adding ezetimibe 10 mg daily - provides additional 15-25% LDL-C reduction.
- Third-line: Consider PCSK9 inhibitors (evolocumab 140 mg or alirocumab 75 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks) - additional 50-60% reduction.
- Alternative agents include inclisiran (284 mg subcutaneously twice yearly), bempedoic acid (180 mg daily), among others.

**Lifestyle Modifications**

- Saturated fat <7% of total calories.
- ≥150 minutes/week moderate-intensity aerobic activity.
- Weight management.

more_info:
**Score interpretation:**

| Stratification | Total Score |
| --- | --- |
| Definite familial hypercholesterolemia | >8 |
| Probable familial hypercholesterolemia | 6-8 |
| Possible familial hypercholesterolemia | 3-5 |
| Unlikely familial hypercholesterolemia | <3 |
